source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וְגַֽם־אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ עַל־אֶפְרַ֣יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לָב֥וֹא לְבֵית־יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת פֶּ֔סַח לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Hezekiah to all Israel and Judah, and also letters he wrote to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to [the] house of Yahweh in Jerusalem to do [a] Passover to Yahweh God of Israel.

en.L: And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem to keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.
en.B: Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters as well to Ephraim and Manasseh, calling them to come to Jerusalem, to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to keep the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: Hezekiah sent messages to all the people of Israel and Judah. He also wrote letters to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh. He invited them to come to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover in honor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: all Israel and Judah; Ephraim and Manasseh: the whole people, the northern tribes included
decisions.reason: Ephraim and Manasseh were the leading tribes of the northern kingdom, which had broken away from David's house (10:16-19). The kings of Assyria had already taken many of its people away (verse 6; 2 Kings 15:29; 17:6). Hezekiah, in his first year (29:3), calls everyone who is left in the north to worship again at the temple in Jerusalem, as one people with Judah.

decisions.choice: a Passover: the yearly feast that remembered the night Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the fourteenth day of the first month and eaten that night (Exodus 12:1-14). The law said it was to be kept at the place Yahweh would choose for his name (Deuteronomy 16:2, 5-6), which is why the people are called to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: sent word ... calling them (Balanced); sent messages ... He invited them (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that Hezekiah "sent" and that the letters were "to come". Balanced and Readable supply what he sent and say plainly that the letters were an invitation. Readable adds "the tribes of" so the names are not read as people, and says "temple" for "house of Yahweh".

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֨ץ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֛יו וְכָל־הַקָּהָ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And took counsel the king and his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem to do the Passover in the month the second.

en.L: And the king and his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month.
en.B: The king, his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem decided to keep the Passover in the second month.
en.R: The king, his leaders and all the people gathered in Jerusalem agreed to celebrate the Passover in the second month.

decisions.choice: in the second month: the law's provision for a later Passover
decisions.reason: The Passover belonged to the first month (Exodus 12:2, 6). Numbers 9:10-11 allowed anyone who was unclean from a dead body or far away on a journey to keep it a month later, on the fourteenth day of the second month. Here the king and the assembly apply that provision to the whole nation, for the reasons given in verse 3.

decisions.choice: took counsel: they consulted together and decided
decisions.reason: The verb means to take advice and come to a decision. The choice was made in council by the king, his officials and the people gathered in Jerusalem, as David consulted the assembly before bringing up the ark (1 Chronicles 13:1-4).

decisions.choice: his princes (Literal); his officials (Balanced); his leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for the king's chief men follows the wording used across these books: "princes", "officials", "leaders".

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יָכְל֛וּ לַעֲשֹׂת֖וֹ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא כִּ֤י הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ לֹֽא־הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמַ דַּ֔יוְהָעָ֖ם לֹא־נֶאֶסְפ֥וּלִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For not they were able to do it at the time the that, for the priests not had consecrated themselves to [what was] enough, and the people not had gathered to Jerusalem.

en.L: For they had not been able to keep it at that time, because the priests had not consecrated themselves in sufficient [number], and the people had not gathered to Jerusalem.
en.B: They had not been able to keep it at the usual time, because too few priests had consecrated themselves and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem.
en.R: They had not been able to celebrate it at the usual time, in the first month. Not enough priests had made themselves holy for the work, and the people had not come together in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: at that time: at the proper time, the fourteenth day of the first month
decisions.reason: "That time" is the time the law set for the Passover (Exodus 12:6; Leviticus 23:5). In Hezekiah's first year the temple was still being cleansed until the sixteenth day of the first month (29:17), so the feast could not be held on the fourteenth.

decisions.choice: had not consecrated themselves in sufficient number: too few priests were ready
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as much as was enough". It is the number of priests that fell short, as 29:34 says: there were too few priests to skin all the burnt offerings, and the Levites had been more careful to consecrate themselves than the priests. To consecrate oneself was to make oneself ritually clean and fit to serve.

decisions.choice: the usual time (Balanced); the usual time, in the first month (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "that time" refers to (m1); Readable names the month.

source.text: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־הַקָּהָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And was right the thing in [the] eyes of the king and in [the] eyes of all the assembly.

en.L: And the thing was right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of all the assembly.
en.B: The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly.
en.R: The king and all the people agreed that this was a good plan.

decisions.choice: was right in the eyes of: seemed good to, was approved by
decisions.reason: "Right in the eyes of" someone means that he judges it right. The king and the whole assembly agreed to the plan of verse 2.

decisions.choice: The plan seemed right to (Balanced); agreed that this was a good plan (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is "thing" or "matter"; here it is the plan to keep the Passover in the second month. Balanced and Readable drop the picture of the eyes.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲמִ֣ידוּ דָבָ֗ר לְהַעֲבִ֨יר ק֤וֹל בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִבְּאֵֽר־שֶׁ֣בַע וְעַד־דָּ֔ן לָב֞וֹא לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּ֛סַח לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָרֹ֛ב עָשׂ֖וּ כַּכָּתֽוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they established [a] word to make pass [a] voice in all Israel from Beersheba and to Dan, to come to do Passover to Yahweh God of Israel in Jerusalem, for not to multitude they had done as written.

en.L: And they established a decree to make a proclamation pass through all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, to come to keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel in Jerusalem, for they had not kept [it] in multitude as [it is] written.
en.B: So they issued a decree to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that the people should come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. For they had not kept it in great numbers, as it is written.
en.R: So they made a decision to send an announcement through all Israel, from Beersheba in the far south to Dan in the far north. The people were to come to Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover in honor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. Not many people had been celebrating it in the way the law says.

decisions.choice: from Beersheba to Dan: the whole land, from its southern edge to its northern edge
decisions.reason: Beersheba was the town at the southern end of the land and Dan the town at the northern end. The usual order is "from Dan to Beersheba" (Judges 20:1; 1 Samuel 3:20; 2 Samuel 17:11). Chronicles turns it round here and in 1 Chronicles 21:2, starting from Judah's end. The call goes to the whole land, north as well as south.

decisions.choice: they had not kept it in great numbers: not by the whole people together
alternatives: they had not kept it for a long time
decisions.reason: The phrase is "not to multitude". Read with verse 13 and verse 26, it means that the Passover had not been kept by all Israel gathered together, as the law intended. It can also mean "not for a long time": the feast had been neglected for many years. Both fit the chapter; the sense of numbers is the more usual one for this phrase.

decisions.choice: as it is written: as the law of Moses prescribes
decisions.reason: The law called for all Israel to keep the Passover together at the place Yahweh would choose (Exodus 12:47; Deuteronomy 16:5-6). "As it is written" refers to that written law; see also verses 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: issued a decree to send a proclamation (Balanced); made a decision to send an announcement (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is "made stand a word to make pass a voice": they settled the matter and sent the call through the land. Readable adds "in the far south" and "in the far north", as at 1 Chronicles 21:2, so a reader knows why the two towns are named.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ הָרָצִ֨ים בָּֽאִגְּר֜וֹת מִיַּ֧ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֗יו בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּכְמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּאֶל־יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָם֙ יִצְחָ֣ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל־הַפְּלֵיטָ֔ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֣רֶת לָכֶ֔ם מִכַּ֖ף מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the runners with the letters from [the] hand of the king and his princes in all Israel and Judah, and according to [the] command of the king, saying, Sons of Israel, return to Yahweh God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and he will return to the escaped [ones], the [ones] remaining to you from [the] palm of [the] kings of Assyria.

en.L: And the runners went with the letters from the hand of the king and his princes through all Israel and Judah, and according to the command of the king, saying, "{{gender:Children|Sons}} of Israel, return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may return to the escaped [ones] who are left to you from the palm of the kings of Assyria.
en.B: The couriers went throughout all Israel and Judah with the letters from the king and his officials. As the king had commanded, they said, "{{gender:Israelites|Sons of Israel}}, return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will return to those of you who are left, who escaped from the grasp of the kings of Assyria.
en.R: The messengers took the letters from the king and his leaders and went through all Israel and Judah. As the king had ordered, they said, "{{gender:Israelites|Sons of Israel}}, come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to you, the few who are left, who escaped from the kings of Assyria.

decisions.choice: the runners: royal couriers
decisions.reason: The word means "those who run". Kings kept runners as guards and messengers (2 Chronicles 12:10-11); here they carry the king's letters through the land.

decisions.choice: return to Yahweh, so that he may return to you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: if the people turn back to Yahweh, he will turn back to them. Verses 8-9 use it again. The prophets make the same call (Zechariah 1:3; Malachi 3:7). To return to Yahweh here means to come back to worship him at his temple and to serve him (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the escaped who are left from the kings of Assyria: the survivors in the north
decisions.reason: Assyrian kings had invaded the northern kingdom more than once. Tiglath-pileser took the people of Galilee and Gilead into exile (2 Kings 15:29), and when Samaria fell the king of Assyria carried Israel away (2 Kings 17:6). The letter speaks to those who were left in the land.

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel: the God of the fathers of all the tribes
decisions.reason: Calling Jacob "Israel" reminds north and south alike that they come from one father and belong to one God, as in David's prayer (1 Chronicles 29:18) and Elijah's (1 Kings 18:36).

decisions.choice: couriers (Balanced); messengers (Readable); the grasp of (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "runners" and "the palm of". Balanced says "couriers" and "the grasp of"; Readable says "messengers" and leaves out the picture of the hand. "Sons of Israel" follows the wording used across these books.

source.text: וְאַל־תִּֽהְי֗וּ כַּאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְכַ֣אֲחֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעֲל֔וּ בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם לְשַׁמָּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתֶּ֥ם רֹאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And not be like your fathers and like your brothers who acted unfaithfully against Yahweh God of their fathers, and he gave them to horror, as you [are] seeing.

en.L: And do not be like your fathers and like your brothers, who acted unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of their fathers, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them up to horror, as you see.
en.B: Do not be like your ancestors and your {{gender:relatives|brothers}}, who were unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them an object of horror, as you see for yourselves.
en.R: Do not be like your ancestors and your {{gender:relatives|brothers}}. They were not loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them be destroyed, and people are shocked at what happened to them, as you can see for yourselves.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully: broke faith with Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to betray a trust, to take what belongs to another. Chronicles uses it for the sin that brought disaster on Saul (1 Chronicles 10:13), on Ahaz (28:19, 22) and on the generation before Hezekiah (29:6).

decisions.choice: gave them up to horror: made them a ruin that appalled those who saw it
decisions.reason: The word means desolation and the horror people feel at the sight of it. Hezekiah used it of Judah's own losses in 29:8; Jeremiah uses it of the land after the exile (Jeremiah 25:9, 18).

decisions.choice: your brothers: the fellow Israelites already taken away
decisions.reason: "Your brothers" are the people of the northern tribes who had been carried off by Assyria (verse 6, verse 9). The word means kin, not only male relatives.

decisions.choice: ancestors (Balanced, Readable); relatives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fathers" and "brothers". Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" and "relatives", with "brothers" as the alternative wording. Readable spells out "object of horror" as what happened and how people reacted.

source.text: עַתָּ֕ה אַל־תַּקְשׁ֥וּ עָרְפְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם תְּנוּ־יָ֣ד לַיהוָ֗ה וּבֹ֤אוּ לְמִקְדָּשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדִּ֣ישׁ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וְעִבְדוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְיָשֹׁ֥ב מִכֶּ֖ם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Now not stiffen your neck like your fathers; give [a] hand to Yahweh and come to his sanctuary which he consecrated forever, and serve Yahweh your God, and will turn from you [the] burning of his anger.

en.L: Now do not stiffen your neck like your fathers; give a hand to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and come to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has consecrated forever, and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, so that the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger may turn from you.
en.B: Now do not stiffen your necks as your ancestors did. Give yourselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and come to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made holy forever. Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger may turn away from you.
en.R: Do not be stubborn, as your ancestors were. Submit to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made holy forever. Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger will turn away from you.

decisions.choice: do not stiffen your neck: do not refuse to obey
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that stiffens its neck against the yoke. The same words describe the northern kingdom's refusal to listen in 2 Kings 17:14, "they stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers"; here the north is urged not to repeat it.

decisions.choice: give a hand to Yahweh: pledge yourselves to him
decisions.reason: To give one's hand was to make a pledge or to submit to someone, as the leaders gave their hand to Solomon (1 Chronicles 29:24) and the men of Ezra's day gave their hand to send away their foreign wives (Ezra 10:19).

decisions.choice: his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever
decisions.reason: Yahweh had told Solomon that he had chosen and consecrated this house so that his name would be there forever (7:16). For northern Israelites, coming to Jerusalem meant leaving the shrines set up by Jeroboam (11:14-15; 13:8-9).

decisions.choice: so that his burning anger may turn from you
decisions.reason: Hezekiah used the same words of Judah in 29:10: the disasters of the past were signs of Yahweh's anger, and turning back to him would turn it away.

decisions.choice: stiffen your necks (Balanced); be stubborn (Readable); give yourselves to (Balanced); submit to (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 17:14, Balanced keeps the picture of the neck and Readable says what it means. Balanced and Readable say what giving a hand means (m2) rather than keep the gesture. Readable says "temple" for "sanctuary".

source.text: כִּ֣י בְשׁוּבְכֶ֞ם עַל־יְהוָ֗ה אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֤ם לְרַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י שֽׁוֹבֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָשׁ֖וּב לָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את כִּֽי־חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹא־יָסִ֤יר פָּנִים֙ מִכֶּ֔ם אִם־תָּשׁ֖וּבוּ אֵלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For in your returning to Yahweh, your brothers and your sons [will be] for compassion before their captors, and to return to the land the this; for gracious and compassionate [is] Yahweh your God, and not he will turn aside face from you if you return to him.

en.L: For when you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your brothers and your sons [will find] compassion before their captors, and [will] return to this land; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] gracious and compassionate, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not turn [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] face from you if you return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: For if you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your {{gender:relatives|brothers}} and your {{gender:children|sons}} will be shown compassion by those who took them captive, and they will come back to this land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is gracious and compassionate, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face away from you if you turn back to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: If you come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the people who took your {{gender:relatives|brothers}} and {{gender:children|sons}} away as prisoners will treat them kindly, and they will be able to come home to this land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is kind and full of mercy. If you come back to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not turn away from you."

decisions.choice: compassion before their captors: as Solomon prayed
decisions.reason: Solomon asked Yahweh to forgive his people when they were taken captive and to "give them compassion before their captors" (1 Kings 8:50; compare 2 Chronicles 6:36-39). The couriers promise that prayer will be answered if the people return.

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate is Yahweh your God
decisions.reason: These are the first words of Yahweh's description of himself to Moses, "a God compassionate and gracious" (Exodus 34:6). Here, as in Psalm 111:4, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2 and Nehemiah 9:17, the two words come in the other order, "gracious and compassionate"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: he will not turn his face from you: he will not reject you
decisions.reason: To turn one's face away is to refuse favor or help; Solomon prayed "do not turn away the face of your anointed" (6:42). Yahweh will receive those who come back.

decisions.choice: your brothers and your sons: family members in exile
decisions.reason: The words mean the people's relatives and children, men and women, who had been carried away (verse 6). Their return depends on the people's own return to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate (Literal, Balanced); kind and full of mercy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep two words close to those of Exodus 34:6. Readable uses plainer words with the same sense, close to its wording at Exodus 34:6. Balanced and Readable give "relatives" and "children", with "brothers" and "sons" as the alternative wording, and Readable turns the captors into the subject of its sentence.

source.text: וַיִּֽהְי֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים עֹבְרִ֨ים מֵעִ֧יר׀לָעִ֛יר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְעַד־זְבֻל֑וּן וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ מַשְׂחִיקִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וּמַלְעִגִ֖ים בָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And were the runners passing from city to city in [the] land of Ephraim and Manasseh and as far as Zebulun, and they were laughing at them and mocking them.

en.L: And the runners were passing from city to city in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun; but they were laughing at them and mocking them.
en.B: The couriers passed from town to town in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh and on as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and mocked them.
en.R: The messengers went from town to town in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far north as Zebulun. But the people there laughed at them and made fun of them.

decisions.choice: as far as Zebulun: into Galilee in the far north
decisions.reason: Ephraim and Manasseh lay in the hill country north of Judah; Zebulun's land was further north, in Galilee. The couriers carried the letter through the whole of what had been the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: laughing at them and mocking them
decisions.reason: Most of the north scorned the call. The same verb for mocking returns at the end of the book, where Judah itself mocks God's messengers until there is no remedy (36:16).

decisions.choice: people (Balanced); the people there (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they were laughing". Balanced and Readable name the people of those towns as the subject, so the couriers are not taken as the ones laughing. Readable adds "north" to show where Zebulun lay.

source.text: אַךְ־אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מֵאָשֵׁ֥ר וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וּמִזְּבֻל֑וּן נִֽכְנְע֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Only men from Asher and Manasseh and from Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

en.L: Only men from Asher and Manasseh and from Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
en.B: Yet some {{gender:people|men}} from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
en.R: But some {{gender:people|men}} from the tribes of Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: only men from Asher ...: yet some did come
decisions.reason: The opening word sets these few against the many who mocked (verse 10). The word for men is the ordinary plural for people; verse 18 shows that whole families from the north ate the Passover.

decisions.choice: humbled themselves: turned from pride to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Humbling oneself is what Yahweh asked of his people in 7:14, and in Chronicles it is the turning point for kings and people alike (12:6-7, 12; 32:26; 33:12). These northerners did what the letter asked (verses 6-9).

decisions.choice: Yet some (Balanced); But some ... the tribes of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "some" for the contrast in m1 and use an inclusive word for the group, with "men" as the alternative wording.

source.text: גַּ֣ם בִּיהוּדָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ יַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֑ד לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Also in Judah was [the] hand of God to give to them heart one to do [the] command of the king and the princes by [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: Also on Judah was the hand of God, to give them one heart to do the command of the king and the princes by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: In Judah too the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to carry out the command of the king and the officials, which followed the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: In Judah, too, God was at work. He made the people united in wanting to do what the king and his leaders had commanded, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

decisions.choice: the hand of God: God's power at work
decisions.reason: The hand of God on a people or a person means his power acting for them, as in Ezra 7:9 and 8:18. Here it moves Judah to agree.

decisions.choice: one heart: a single, united will
decisions.reason: To have one heart is to be of one mind and purpose, as the warriors who came to make David king were "of one heart" (1 Chronicles 12:39).

decisions.choice: the command of the king ... by the word of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The king's command was not his own idea only; it followed what Yahweh had commanded in his law, as the temple service Hezekiah restored was "by the word of Yahweh" (29:15, 25).

decisions.choice: was at work (Balanced); God was at work (Readable); the officials (Balanced); his leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of God's hand means (m1). Readable says "united in wanting" for "one heart". The word for the king's chief men follows the wording used in verse 2.

source.text: וַיֵּֽאָסְפ֤וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַם־רָ֔ב לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת אֶת־חַ֥ג הַמַּצּ֖וֹת בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י קָהָ֖ל לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered [at] Jerusalem people many to do the festival of the unleavened [bread] in the month the second, an assembly great very.

en.L: And many people gathered [at] Jerusalem to keep the festival of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great assembly.
en.B: A great crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very large assembly.
en.R: A huge crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem in the second month to celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. It was a very large gathering.

decisions.choice: the festival of unleavened bread: the seven days of eating bread made without yeast
decisions.reason: The Passover on the fourteenth day was followed by seven days when no yeast was eaten (Exodus 12:15-20; Leviticus 23:5-8). Here the name covers the whole celebration, the Passover included (verse 15), as the two were kept together.

decisions.choice: a very great assembly: the crowd met as Israel's gathered assembly
decisions.reason: The word is the same "assembly" as in verses 2 and 4. The Passover of verse 5, which had not been kept "in multitude", is now kept by a great assembly.

decisions.choice: the Festival of Unleavened Bread (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the name of the feast with capitals, as at 8:13.

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֕מוּ וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ֙ אֶת־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַֽמְקַטְּרוֹת֙ הֵסִ֔ירוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֖יכוּ לְנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they arose and removed the altars which [were] in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they removed and threw [them] into [the] wadi of Kidron.

en.L: And they arose and removed the altars that [were] in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they removed, and they threw [them] into the Wadi Kidron.
en.B: They set to work and removed the altars in Jerusalem. They also removed all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.
en.R: The people went to work and took away the altars in Jerusalem. They also removed all the altars for burning incense and threw them into the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: the altars in Jerusalem and the incense altars: those set up by Ahaz
decisions.reason: Hezekiah's father Ahaz had made altars for himself in every corner of Jerusalem and high places in every town of Judah to burn incense to other gods (28:24-25). Before the feast the people cleared them away.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Kidron: the valley on the east side of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that runs in the rainy season. The Kidron was where unclean things were thrown out and destroyed: Asa burned his mother's idol there (15:16), and the Levites carried the filth of the temple there (29:16).

decisions.choice: they arose: they set to work
decisions.reason: "Arose" here marks the start of an action, not standing up.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Kidron (Literal); the Kidron Valley (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 15:16. Readable says "altars for burning incense" so the word is clear.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם נִכְלְמוּ֙ וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ עֹל֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they slaughtered the Passover on [the] fourteen of the month the second, and the priests and the Levites were ashamed and consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings [to the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth [day] of the second month. And the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings [into] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. Ashamed, the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: On the fourteenth day of the second month they killed the lambs for the Passover. The priests and Levites felt ashamed, so they made themselves holy and brought burnt offerings to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover animal
decisions.reason: "The Passover" can name the animal killed for the feast, as in Exodus 12:21, "slaughter the Passover". It was a lamb or a young goat (Exodus 12:5).

decisions.choice: the priests and the Levites were ashamed: put to shame by the people's readiness
decisions.reason: The chapter does not say why. The most likely reason is that the people came eagerly while too few priests had made themselves ready (verse 3; 29:34). Their shame moved them to consecrate themselves at once.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings: the offerings the law required on each day of the feast
decisions.reason: Numbers 28:16-25 lists burnt offerings for every day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Once consecrated, the priests and Levites could present them.

decisions.choice: the Passover lamb (Balanced); the lambs for the Passover (Readable); made themselves holy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the animal (m1). Readable says "made themselves holy" for "consecrated themselves", as at 5:11, and "temple" for "house".

source.text: וַיַּֽעַמְד֤וּ עַל־עָמְדָם֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם כְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ זֹרְקִ֣ים אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם מִיַּ֖ד הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they stood at their place according to their ordinance, according to [the] law of Moses [the] man of God; the priests [were] throwing the blood from [the] hand of the Levites.

en.L: And they stood at their station according to their ordinance, according to the law of Moses the man of God; the priests [were] throwing the blood [received] from the hand of the Levites.
en.B: They took their usual places as the law of Moses the man of God prescribes, and the priests splashed the blood that they received from the Levites.
en.R: They stood in their places, as the law of Moses, the man of God, required. The Levites handed the blood to the priests, and the priests splashed it on the altar.

decisions.choice: their station according to their ordinance: their assigned places and duties
decisions.reason: The word for ordinance can mean a rule or an established custom. Each group stood where its duty placed it at the altar.

decisions.choice: Moses the man of God
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet. Moses is given it in Deuteronomy 33:1 and 1 Chronicles 23:14.

decisions.choice: the priests threw the blood received from the Levites
decisions.reason: The blood of an offering was thrown against the altar by the priests (Leviticus 1:5). Here the Levites, who had slaughtered the animals for many of the people (verse 17), handed the blood to the priests.

decisions.choice: throwing (Literal); splashed (Balanced, Readable); on the altar (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at Leviticus 1:5. Readable says where the blood went, which the law takes for granted.

source.text: כִּי־רַבַּ֥ת בַּקָּהָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם עַל־שְׁחִיטַ֣ת הַפְּסָחִ֗ים לְכֹל֙ לֹ֣א טָה֔וֹר לְהַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For many [were] in the assembly who not had consecrated themselves, and the Levites [were] over [the] slaughtering of the Passovers for everyone not clean, to consecrate [them] to Yahweh.

en.L: For [there were] many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves; and the Levites [were] over the slaughtering of the Passovers for everyone [who was] not clean, to consecrate [them] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Since many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, the Levites took charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for all who were not clean, to consecrate them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Many people in the crowd had not made themselves holy. So the Levites had the job of killing the Passover lambs for everyone who was not ritually clean, so that the lambs would be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Levites were over the slaughtering: they killed the lambs for those who were unclean
decisions.reason: Normally the head of each household killed the family's Passover lamb (Exodus 12:6, 21). Someone who was ritually unclean could not do so without making the offering unclean, so the Levites did it for them.

decisions.choice: to consecrate them: the lambs
alternatives: to consecrate the people to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. It most likely means the lambs, which the Levites killed so that they would be holy offerings to Yahweh. It could mean the people, whom the Levites helped to keep the feast in holiness.

decisions.choice: not clean: ritually unclean
decisions.reason: Being unclean was a state, not a sin, brought about by things such as touching a dead body (Numbers 9:6). The law kept the unclean from holy things until they were cleansed.

decisions.choice: [them] (Literal); them (Balanced); the lambs (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced supply a pronoun; Readable names the lambs, following m2.

source.text: כִּ֣י מַרְבִּ֣ית הָעָ֡ם רַ֠בַּת מֵֽאֶפְרַ֨יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה יִשָּׂשכָ֤ר וּזְבֻלוּן֙ לֹ֣א הִטֶּהָ֔רוּ כִּֽי־אָכְל֥וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֖סַח בְּלֹ֣א כַכָּת֑וּב כִּי֩ הִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב יְכַפֵּ֥ר בְּעַֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] greater part of the people, many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, not had purified themselves, for they ate the Passover not as written; for prayed Hezekiah for them, saying, Yahweh the good may make atonement for

en.L: For a multitude of the people, many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover not as [it is] written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the good [one], make atonement for
en.B: A large part of the people, many of them from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, and yet they ate the Passover in a way that did not keep to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is good, pardon
en.R: Many of the people, a large number of them from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not made themselves clean. Even so, they ate the Passover, which was not what the law said. But Hezekiah prayed for them. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} forgive

decisions.choice: they ate the Passover not as written: while still unclean
decisions.reason: The law said that anyone unclean who ate a holy offering would be cut off from the people (Leviticus 7:20-21), and those unclean at Passover were to wait for the second month (Numbers 9:6-11). Many of the northerners had come too late or did not know the rules of cleansing, and they ate unclean.

decisions.choice: for ... for: yet they ate ... but Hezekiah prayed
decisions.reason: The same small word joins three clauses. The second marks what they did in spite of being unclean; the third explains why no harm followed: Hezekiah prayed for them, and Yahweh heard (verse 20).

decisions.choice: make atonement for: pardon
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for making atonement by sacrifice. With Yahweh himself as the one who acts, it means to cover the wrong and pardon it, as in Deuteronomy 21:8 and Psalm 78:38. Hezekiah asks Yahweh to do what no rite had done.

decisions.choice: Yahweh, the good one: the prayer rests on his goodness
decisions.reason: The prayer calls on Yahweh by what he is. "Yahweh is good" was the song at the temple's dedication (5:13; 7:3; 1 Chronicles 16:34).

decisions.choice: make atonement for (Literal); pardon (Balanced); forgive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the usual wording for this verb. Balanced and Readable say what it means when God is the one who acts (m3). Hezekiah's sentence runs on into verse 19, so this record ends in the middle of it.

source.text: כָּל־לְבָב֣וֹ הֵכִ֔ין לִדְר֛וֹשׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֥ים׀יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֖א כְּטָהֳרַ֥ת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: everyone [who] his heart has set to seek the God, Yahweh God of his fathers, and not according to [the] purification of the holy [place].

en.L: everyone [who] has set his heart to seek God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of his fathers, though not according to the purification of the sanctuary."
en.B: everyone who sets {{gender:their|his}} heart on seeking God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of {{gender:their|his}} ancestors, even if {{gender:they are|he is}} not clean as the sanctuary requires."
en.R: everyone who has made up {{gender:their|his}} mind to seek God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of {{gender:their|his}} ancestors, even if {{gender:they are|he is}} not clean by the rules of the holy temple."

decisions.choice: has set his heart to seek God: is determined to seek him
decisions.reason: To set the heart is to direct one's will, as Jehoshaphat "set his heart to seek God" (19:3). To seek God in Chronicles is to turn to him in worship and obedience.

decisions.choice: though not according to the purification of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Hezekiah asks that those whose hearts are set on God be pardoned even though they lack the ritual cleanness the holy place requires. The rules of cleanness are not set aside; the prayer asks for mercy where they were broken.

decisions.choice: everyone ... his heart: any person, man or woman
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular and masculine because it follows "everyone"; the prayer is for all the people who ate (verse 18).

decisions.choice: their (default); his (alternative)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "their" for "everyone" (m3), with "his" as the alternative wording. Literal keeps the Hebrew pronoun. Readable says "made up their mind" for setting the heart, as at 19:3.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּרְפָּ֖א אֶת־הָעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And listened Yahweh to Hezekiah and healed the people.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard Hezekiah and healed the people.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Hezekiah's prayer and healed the people.

decisions.choice: Yahweh heard ... and healed: the promise of 7:14 kept
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised Solomon that if his people humbled themselves, prayed and sought him, he would hear from heaven, forgive their sin and heal their land (7:14). The northerners humbled themselves (verse 11), sought God (verse 19) and Hezekiah prayed for them; now Yahweh hears and heals.

decisions.choice: healed the people: spared them and made them whole
alternatives: he cured an illness that had come on them
decisions.reason: The law warned that uncleanness near Yahweh's dwelling brought death (Leviticus 15:31). Healing may mean that Yahweh kept the people from sickness or harm that their eating unclean could bring, or that he forgave them and restored them to himself, as healing is used in 7:14 and Hosea 14:5. The verse does not say that anyone had fallen ill.

decisions.choice: listened to (Literal); heard (Balanced); answered Hezekiah's prayer (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means both to hear and to respond. Readable says plainly that Yahweh did what Hezekiah asked.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶת־חַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וּֽמְהַלְלִ֣ים לַ֠יהוָה י֣וֹם׀בְּי֞וֹם הַלְוִיִּ֧ם וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים בִּכְלֵי־עֹ֖ז לַיהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel the [ones] present in Jerusalem the festival of the unleavened [bread] seven days with joy great, and praising Yahweh day by day the Levites and the priests with instruments of strength to Yahweh.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the festival of unleavened bread seven days with great joy, and the Levites and the priests [were] praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} day by day with instruments of strength to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were present in Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, while the Levites and the priests praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} day after day, playing loud instruments for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were in Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days, and they were full of joy. Every day the Levites and priests praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, playing loud instruments to honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: with instruments of strength to Yahweh: loud instruments played for him
alternatives: praising Yahweh with all their strength
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "with instruments of strength". A very similar phrase, "with all strength", describes David's worship before the ark (1 Chronicles 13:8), and some read that here by a small change of letters: "praising Yahweh with all their strength". The record follows the Hebrew text. Either way the praise was loud and wholehearted.

decisions.choice: who were present: those who were found there
decisions.reason: The word means "those who were found" in Jerusalem: everyone who had come, from the north and the south alike.

decisions.choice: the Levites and the priests praising Yahweh
decisions.reason: Hezekiah had restored the Levite singers and players with the instruments of David and the priests with trumpets (29:25-28), as David had set them in order (1 Chronicles 15:16; 16:4-6).

decisions.choice: loud instruments (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "instruments of strength". Balanced and Readable say what the phrase describes, the sound of the music. Readable uses "him" for the second mention of the divine name.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עַל־לֵב֙ כָּל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַמַּשְׂכִּילִ֥ים שֵֽׂכֶל־ט֖וֹב לַיהוָ֑ה וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ אֶת־הַמּוֹעֵד֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים מְזַבְּחִים֙ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֔ים וּמִ֨תְוַדִּ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Hezekiah to [the] heart of all the Levites the [ones] showing understanding good to Yahweh, and they ate the appointed [feast] seven the days, sacrificing sacrifices of peace offerings and giving thanks to Yahweh God of their fathers.

en.L: And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who showed good understanding toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And they ate the appointed feast seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of peace offerings and giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of their fathers.
en.B: Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good skill in the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For the seven days of the festival they ate the festival meals, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.
en.R: Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites, who had shown such good skill in serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For seven days the people ate the festival meals. They offered peace offerings and thanked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: spoke to the heart of: encouraged, spoke kindly to
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak to comfort or encourage, as Joseph did to his brothers (Genesis 50:21) and Hezekiah to his officers (32:6); compare Isaiah 40:2.

decisions.choice: who showed good understanding toward Yahweh: skilled in his service
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean skill in leading the worship and music, or insight in teaching the people, as the Levites later explained the law (Nehemiah 8:7-8). Either way Hezekiah commends Levites who served Yahweh well.

decisions.choice: they ate the appointed feast: ate the meals of the festival
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they "ate the appointed feast", meaning the meals of the festival, chiefly the meat of the peace offerings. The ancient Greek translation reads "they completed the feast", from a word that differs by one letter. The record follows the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: or making confession
decisions.reason: The verb means to acknowledge, either praising Yahweh with thanks or confessing sin before him (Ezra 10:11; Nehemiah 9:3). With peace offerings, and in a week of joy, thanksgiving is the more likely sense.

decisions.choice: the festival meals (Balanced, Readable); the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "ate the appointed feast" refers to (m3). Readable names the people as the ones who ate, since the whole assembly kept the feast (verse 23). Readable says "encouraged" for the idiom in m1.

source.text: וַיִּוָּֽעֲצוּ֙ כָּל־הַקָּהָ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ שִׁבְעַת־יָמִ֖ים שִׂמְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took counsel all the assembly to do seven days other, and they did seven days [with] joy.

en.L: And all the assembly took counsel to keep another seven days, and they kept seven days [with] joy.
en.B: Then the whole assembly decided to keep the festival for another seven days, and they kept seven more days with joy.
en.R: Then all the people decided to celebrate for seven more days. So they celebrated another seven days, full of joy.

decisions.choice: another seven days: as at the dedication of Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: At the dedication of the temple Solomon and all Israel celebrated for seven days and then seven more (7:8-9; 1 Kings 8:65). This second week brings that feast to mind, as verse 26 says outright.

decisions.choice: took counsel: the assembly decided together
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 2, where the king, his officials and the assembly made the first decision. Now the whole assembly decides on its own to go on.

decisions.choice: the festival (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "to do another seven days". Balanced supplies what was kept; Readable says "celebrate".

source.text: כִּ֣י חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְ֠הוּדָה הֵרִ֨ים לַקָּהָ֜ל אֶ֣לֶף פָּרִים֮ וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֣ים צֹאן֒סוְהַשָּׂרִ֞ים הֵרִ֤ימוּ לַקָּהָל֙ פָּרִ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֖אן עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ כֹהֲנִ֖ים לָרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed for the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the princes contributed for the assembly bulls a thousand and sheep ten thousand; and consecrated themselves priests in multitude.

en.L: For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep, and the princes contributed to the assembly 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep; and priests consecrated themselves in multitude.
en.B: Hezekiah king of Judah provided 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for the assembly, and the officials provided 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep. A great number of priests consecrated themselves.
en.R: King Hezekiah of Judah gave the people 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats, and the leaders gave them 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep and goats. And many priests made themselves holy.

decisions.choice: contributed: set aside as a gift for the offerings
decisions.reason: The verb means "lifted up", used of setting something apart as a gift for holy use. Josiah and his officials later gave animals to the people for the Passover in the same way (35:7-8). Most of these animals were peace offerings, eaten by the worshipers (verse 22).

decisions.choice: sheep: animals of the flock
decisions.reason: The word means the flock, which takes in both sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: priests consecrated themselves in multitude: now there were enough
decisions.reason: The same phrase as in verse 5 for numbers. In the first month there were too few consecrated priests (verse 3); now a great number of them were ready to serve.

decisions.choice: sheep (Literal, Balanced); sheep and goats (Readable); princes, officials, leaders
decisions.reason: Readable names both animals of the flock (m2). The word for the king's chief men follows the wording used in verse 2.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֣וּ׀כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֗ה וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְכָל־הַקָּהָ֖ל הַבָּאִ֣ים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַגֵּרִ֗ים הַבָּאִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַיּוֹשְׁבִ֖ים בִּיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And rejoiced all [the] assembly of Judah and the priests and the Levites and all the assembly the [ones] coming from Israel, and the sojourners the [ones] coming from [the] land of Israel and the [ones] dwelling in Judah.

en.L: And all the assembly of Judah rejoiced, and the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the sojourners who came from the land of Israel and who dwelt in Judah.
en.B: The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, together with the priests and the Levites, the whole assembly that had come from Israel, and the outsiders who had come from the land of Israel or who lived in Judah.
en.R: All the people of Judah were full of joy. So were the priests and Levites, all the people who had come from Israel, and the outsiders who had come from the land of Israel or who lived in Judah.

decisions.choice: the sojourners: foreigners living among Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone of another people who had settled in Israel. The law let a sojourner keep the Passover if the males of the household were circumcised, under the same law as an Israelite (Exodus 12:48-49; Numbers 9:14).

decisions.choice: and those who dwelt in Judah: sojourners living in Judah
decisions.reason: The last phrase most likely names a second group of sojourners: some came from the north, others lived in Judah. It could instead name the people of Judah again, but they have already been named at the start of the verse.

decisions.choice: all the assembly: one people rejoicing together
decisions.reason: Judah, the priests and Levites, the northern tribes and the foreigners among them rejoiced together. For a time the divided people worshiped as one.

decisions.choice: sojourners (Literal); outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for a resident foreigner follows the wording used across these books.

source.text: וַתְּהִ֥י שִׂמְחָֽה־גְדוֹלָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֠י מִימֵ֞י שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן־דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א כָזֹ֖את בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And there was joy great in Jerusalem, for from [the] days of Solomon son of David king of Israel not like this in Jerusalem.

en.L: And there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel [there had been] nothing like this in Jerusalem.
en.B: So there was great joy in Jerusalem, because nothing like this had happened in Jerusalem since the time of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.
en.R: Jerusalem was full of joy. Nothing like this had happened there since the time of King Solomon, David's son, who ruled all Israel.

decisions.choice: since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel
decisions.reason: Solomon was the last king over all twelve tribes, and at the dedication of the temple all Israel feasted together for fourteen days (7:8-10). Since the kingdom split (chapter 10) the north and the south had not worshiped together in Jerusalem like this. The comparison is about the gathering and its joy; Josiah's Passover is said to surpass all others since the days of Samuel (35:18).

decisions.choice: nothing like this: the verb is left out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "not like this", leaving the reader to supply "there had been".

decisions.choice: who ruled all Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "king of Israel" here as king over the whole undivided people, since elsewhere in the book Israel names the northern kingdom.

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשָּׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם וַתָּב֧וֹא תְפִלָּתָ֛ם לִמְע֥וֹן קָדְשׁ֖וֹ לַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And arose the priests the Levites and blessed the people, and was heard their voice, and came their prayer to [the] dwelling of his holiness, to the heavens.

en.L: And the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling, to the heavens.
en.B: Then the Levitical priests stood and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer reached heaven, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling place.
en.R: Then the priests, who were from the tribe of Levi, stood up and blessed the people. God heard them. Their prayer reached heaven, the holy place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

decisions.choice: the priests the Levites: the Levitical priests
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "the priests the Levites", the phrase Deuteronomy uses for the priests as members of the tribe of Levi (Deuteronomy 18:1; compare 2 Chronicles 5:5; 23:18). Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "the priests and the Levites", as in verses 15, 21 and 25. The record follows the Hebrew text; blessing the people was the priests' task (Numbers 6:23-27).

decisions.choice: their prayer came to his holy dwelling, to heaven
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 26:15 prays, "Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven", and Solomon asked Yahweh to hear from heaven, his dwelling place, every prayer made toward the temple (6:21, 30). The chapter ends with that prayer answered.

decisions.choice: their voice was heard: God heard them
decisions.reason: The verb is passive and does not name who heard. The next clause shows it was Yahweh in heaven.

decisions.choice: God heard them (Readable); the priests, who were from the tribe of Levi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who heard (m3) and explains "the priests the Levites" (m1). Balanced says "the Levitical priests".
